li_projects.title: Splice — KV-cache editing for long-context LLMs
li_projects.description: When an AI agent's context is trimmed, Splice edits the model's KV cache in place instead of re-processing everything after the edit. Built at Brevitas. • 3.1x lower wall-clock per edit at 72B on 2x H100 (1.65x including one-time setup), with output quality held within a KL budget of a fresh re-ingest • Built as an SGLang radix-cache backend: 2.75x faster than SGLang re-prefill with 25% of a 16k c

li_projects.title: Bricked — Finalist, Hack the North 2026
li_projects.description: Finalist at Hack the North 2026. Describe anything in plain English and Bricked designs it in Lego, then generates step-by-step build instructions and a link to buy the parts. • LLMs can't place 3D parts reliably, so GPT generates concept art, Claude turns it into shapes and proportions, and a Python solver converts that geometry into real LDraw parts • A critic model refines each build using 3D r

li_projects.title: Open source — LMCache and MemOS contributions
li_projects.description: Bug fixes to two ~11k-star LLM infrastructure projects, each with a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after. • LMCache (KV-cache library used by vLLM, SGLang and NVIDIA Dynamo), PR #4599, merged: one timed-out benchmark round crashed the results summary or understated throughput by 20%. Timed-out rounds now get their own counter, plus the module's first unit tests • MemOS (memor

li_projects.title: OpenDrone — McGill AeroHacks 2026
li_projects.description: Indoor navigation for drones, built at McGill University's drone hackathon. Indoor spaces have no GPS, so OpenDrone maps a building with a drone, reconstructs it in 3D with Gaussian splatting, and lets you navigate or query the space by voice in natural language (27 languages).

li_projects.title: Slicefund — Best Use of Solana, Hack Canada 2026
li_projects.description: Best Use of Solana at Hack Canada 2026. Index funds for prediction markets, spanning 7,000+ markets on Polymarket, Kalshi and Manifold. • 4 AI agents find combinatorial arbitrage across the three platforms, using embedding matching to spot the same market listed in different places • Tiered caching keeps cross-platform spread detection live; fund shares are minted as Solana SPL tokens

li_projects.title: BioBuddy AI — Spur Accelerator, University of Waterloo
li_projects.description: On-device wildlife and threat detection, built through the Spur Accelerator at the University of Waterloo. • Trained a ResNet-18 from scratch on 2,500 images across 8 classes to 90%+ accuracy • Cut inference from 800 ms to 200 ms with TorchScript, running 30 fps camera capture, LiDAR and offline voice recognition on the same Raspberry Pi 4

li_projects.title: Ferdinand — 1st Overall, Hack the Ridge 2025
li_projects.description: 1st Overall at Hack the Ridge 2025. A voice-controlled AI agent that turns speech into multi-step computer actions, built for people with physical disabilities who struggle to use a mouse and keyboard. • Claude reads the screen to find what to click, GPT-4o breaks each request into steps, and PyAutoGUI carries them out • Completed 92% of 50 test tasks

li_projects.title: SimTeach — Best Use of AI, PennApps XXVI
li_projects.description: Best Use of AI at PennApps XXVI (University of Pennsylvania). Trains teachers with realistic, AI-generated classroom scenarios and gives instant feedback on how they handled them, so they can practise without real students at stake.

li_projects.title: Seizure Seeker — EEG seizure detection research
li_projects.description: Research at the Science Mentorship Institute with a Harvard PhD mentor. A model that flags intractable epileptic seizures from EEG recordings. • 1-second windows at 50% overlap, RMS features, and z-score thresholding (RMS > median + z·MAD) • A merge/filter pass cuts false positives • Presented at the Sci-Mi Symposium to 500+ attendees

posts.text: How did two high school students end up in the newspaper at the biggest AI engineering fair? Wild week. Anish Paleja and I volunteered with Major League Hacking, with Mike Swift, at the AI Engineer World's Fair. We met some of the coolest people and attended the coolest events. We planned to hand out newspapers on the show floor and meet people. Ended up being one of the best decisions we made this summer. Anish Paleja and I just got into Founders, Inc. Off Season II 🚀 Two high schoolers from Toronto, moving to San Francisco this summer to build out of the world's biggest founder campus at Fort Mason. A year ago, if you'd told me this is how we'd be spending our summer, I genuinely wouldn't have believed you.
